diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: L1=k; L2=RGamma(P1,k)[1] is k[1] direct sum k[-1]. Upper arrows alpha:k to L2[-1] and beta[-1]:L2[-1] to k; lower arrows beta:L2 to k[1] and alpha[1]:k[1] to L2.
diagram_math_checks.relations_checked: Step 2.1 identifies alpha with H0 inclusion and beta[-1] with its projection, so beta[-1] circle alpha=id_k. F2 and step 3.1 identify this source-first product with alpha*beta. In the lower row alpha[1] circle beta is an endomorphism of L2, identity on k[1] and zero on k[-1], so it is nonzero and differs from id_L2. The projector label denotes this endomorphism, as explained in the preceding prose.

diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: Complex surface P1 times P1 contains the complex curves P1 times {i} and Delta_P1. Their intersection is (i,i). i:pt to P1 and a:P1 to pt are defined in the adjacent prose; h sends the matched middle point to Z11=pt.
diagram_math_checks.relations_checked: In a holomorphic coordinate centered at i, quotient normal coordinate z1-z2 restricts on the horizontal complex curve to z1, a complex-linear isomorphism with positive real determinant. Thus transverse diagonal Thom intersection has coefficient +1. The input fundamental class and point class have BM degrees 2 and 0; Delta! lowers by 2d2=2, giving degree zero, and proper h_* sends the positive point class to [pt]. The diagram explicitly calls the crossing schematic; it represents complex curves, not real dimensions.
